punch: And the mechanism explains why recovery isn't guaranteed.

headline: Suppression gets discussed
body: Come off, restart the axis, recover. The framing is that shutdown is temporary and reversible by default.
punch: The tissue-level data is less relaxed about it.

headline: The protocol
body: Nandrolone decanoate, twice weekly, for ten weeks in male rats. High dose — and the point is what high dose does to tissue, not what typical use does.

headline: The damage
body: Destruction of the basement epithelial lining. Tubular degeneration and necrosis in the testis and epididymis. Severe histopathological change, not just altered hormone levels.
punch: Architecture damaged, not only signalling suppressed.

headline: The mechanism
body: Exogenous nandrolone suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis. LH and FSH fall. Intratesticular testosterone falls with them.
punch: The testis runs on a signal the drug switches off.

headline: Then it cascades
body: Fewer Sertoli cells. Reduced spermatogonia. Falling intratesticular testosterone — which the testis needs at concentrations far above blood levels to function at all.
punch: Blood testosterone can look fine while the testis starves.

headline: Which is why
body: Signalling suppression reverses when the drug stops. Cell loss and structural damage are a different category, and the two are routinely discussed as if they're one.
punch: Suppressed and damaged have different endings.

headline: And the age factor
body: Anyone using these for height still has open growth plates, meaning a reproductive axis that hasn't finished maturing — being suppressed before it completed.
punch: Interrupting a system mid-construction isn't the same as pausing a finished one.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
